column1: # The parity matrix of Desk Slides: every row of the survey of Keynote '09,
# each with the phase of the roadmap of Desk Slides that completes it
# (- when out of scope). The shared column names the rows of the other
# surveys that describe the same feature, or says the feature is only
# of Keynote. The KGNM rows are what the GNOME HIG and desktop ask, and
# the KVMI rows are the commands that the inventory of Keynote on the
# reference virtual machine added to the survey.
# Tab-separated; the survey, the roadmap and the inventory of 2026-11-14
# The gnome column says how Desk adapts a row to GNOME where the
# 2026-11-16 (window M+, D-008, and automatic saving) changed its form; the row passes
# when Desk does it that way.

column4: expected
column8: gnome

column4: Opens when the app starts and with File > New from Theme Chooser (Shift-Cmd-N). Moving the pointer slowly over a theme runs through sample slides with charts, tables and text. The Slide Size menu is in the chooser itself.
column8: A theme gallery inside the empty window, without a window of its own, like the template gallery of Desk Writer (path E)

column4: A theme is a set of masters with matching fonts, backgrounds, textures, table styles and chart colors. New text, shapes, tables and charts take the style of the theme. The theme can be changed later, and a document can mix several. The details are in the section on masters and themes.
column7: Partial: the theme as a set

column4: Almost every theme has Title & Subtitle, Title & Bullets, Title & Bullets – 2 Column, Bullets, Blank, Title – Top or Center, Photo – Horizontal, Photo – Vertical, Title, Bullets & Photo, and Title & Bullets – Left or Right.

The title and body of every new slide show "Double-click to edit" (Zum Bearbeiten doppelklicken) already with the final appearance, including the bullets of the body. A picture, PDF or movie dragged onto the media placeholder takes its size, position and frame. Outside the placeholder, media do not inherit these attributes.
Slide canvas in the middle, slide navigator on the left, presenter notes field below, toolbar and format bar. The View menu shows or hides each part.
column8: M+: slide navigator in the navigation sidebar, presenter notes under the slide, from the View menu, and the Play button in the header bar

column4: View > Zoom and a menu at the bottom left corner of the slide canvas.
column8: M+: a zoom control overlaid on a corner of the slide, besides the View menu

column4: Thumbnails of all the slides, with a size control at the bottom left corner. Dragging reorders and indents slides. Duplicate, copy and paste work on one or several contiguous slides. Dragging the top control down, or View > Show Masters, opens the list of masters.
column8: M+: the Navigator page of the navigation sidebar; the masters are another page of it

column4: Shows the title and bullets of each slide as readable and editable text. Dragging a bullet changes its level or moves it to another slide, and a double click on the slide icon collapses the bullets. The outline font is in Preferences, and the outline can be printed. The text comes from the title and body placeholders, which in ODP are presentation:class title and outline.
column8: M+: the Outline page of the navigation sidebar

column4: A grid of larger thumbnails to rearrange by dragging, with an adjustable size. A double click opens the slide. Adding, deleting, duplicating and skipping slides work as in the Navigator.
column8: M+: takes the document area, from the View menu, with the thumbnail size control overlaid on it

column4: View > Slide Only hides the navigator. Lion full screen uses the corner button or the View menu, and Esc leaves it.
column8: F11 enters and leaves full screen

column4: Click the thumbnail in the Navigator or the Outline, or Slide > Go To > Next, Previous, First or Last.
column8: M+: the slide thumbnails are in the navigation sidebar, and the Slide menu of the navigator has Go To

column4: Customizable as in Pages. Default buttons: New (slide), Play, View, Themes, Masters, Text Box, Shape, Table, Chart, Comment, Share (iWork.com), Mask, Alpha, Front, Back, Inspector, Media, Colors and Fonts, plus Full Screen on Lion.
column8: Header bar of M+ (D-008): at the start, the Sidebar button, the Insert menu and the six object buttons Table, Chart, Text, Shape, Media and Comment; the window title in the middle, with the folder as subtitle; at the end, Open documents, Find, Inspector and the main menu. No customization (path A), plus the Play button, which has a menu (from the start, from this slide, rehearse, record, presenter display). New slide is the + button of the sidebar, Themes is in the Document pane, and Masters, Mask, Alpha, Front and Back are in the Format pane

column4: Changes with the selection. With a shape or text box: font, typeface, size and color, alignment, line spacing, number of columns, background color, borders, opacity and shadow. With a table: rows and columns, cell text, alignment, borders, headers and footers, and background color.
column8: M+: there is no format bar. With an object, the Format pane has style, stroke, shadow, reflection, opacity, Adjust image, Edit mask, Instant alpha and Arrange; with nothing selected, master, background and Skip this slide

column4: Document, Slide, Build (Animation), Text, Graphic (Grafik), Metrics, Table, Chart (Diagramm), Hyperlink and QuickTime. Several windows can be open. Slide and Build take the place of the Layout and Wrap panes of Pages.
column8: A single Inspector, in the sidebar, as in Desk Writer (path C). In M+ the choice at the top of the pane is Format, Animate and Document: Animate has In, Action and Out for the selected object, or the slide transition with nothing selected; Document has Document, Audio and Info

column4: The same as in Pages.
column8: Media as a popover of the Media button, Fonts and Colors as popovers, as in Desk Writer (path D and M+)

column4: Lists what was not imported or exported correctly and the warnings when saving to an earlier version. Lets the user replace a missing font and copy the warnings.
column8: A banner with See warnings and the list in a dialog, as in Desk Writer (path I)

column4: A list of shortcuts in Help. Control-click opens the context menu, on the slide canvas too.
column8: Context menu from the right button, the Menu key and Shift+F10; the GNOME shortcuts dialog

column4: Onscreen help, video tutorials, help tags when the pointer rests, and the iWork formulas and functions guide in the Help menu.
column8: Help in the GNOME format, opened with F1

column4: File > New from Theme Chooser, choice of theme and slide size, and Choose or a double click. Changing the size later resizes all the content of the slides.
The General preference "Use theme" always opens the chosen theme instead of the Chooser.
File > Open or drag onto the app icon. Keeps text, colors, layout and as much of the formatting as possible.
Double click, drag onto the icon, File > Open, Recent Items, or Open an Existing File and Recent in the Chooser. Asks for the password when there is one.
Missing fonts are replaced with an installed one. Missing movies and sounds have to be inserted again. A Keynote '08 document can stay in the '08 format when saved.

Images and chart data go in the file, fonts do not. Audio and movies go inside the document by default. "Include preview in document" makes the thumbnail, and "Save a copy as" writes Keynote '08 or PowerPoint.
Copy audio and movies into the document or only link them, and copy the theme images or not. Without them, the presentation changes on a computer that does not have the theme.

column3: Automatic saving, versions and backup copy
column4: On Lion, saves by itself, and Cmd-S keeps a version. Browse All Versions restores the whole presentation or lets the user copy objects, settings and text from an old version. The "Back up previous version" preference keeps only the previous version.
column8: Automatic saving and versions, as in iWork 15 (D-001): the document saves itself, and the versions are browsed and restored from the main menu

column4: Creates an untitled copy opened next to the original (on Snow Leopard, Save As).
File > Save Theme keeps the presentation as a theme, which then appears in the Theme Chooser.
Author, keywords and comments in the Document Inspector, for Spotlight.
From the window title menu, on Lion. Prevents accidental editing until the user unlocks it.
Unlimited undo since opening and File > Revert to Saved.
Require password to open in the Document Inspector, with the Password Assistant. The hint appears after three wrong tries, and the Numbers guide says two, which is to be checked on the VM.

Require password to exit show in the Document Inspector. To stop, the name and password of an administrator of the computer running the presentation are needed, not a document password. On GNOME, the equivalent is a polkit authentication.
With Option, closes all. Asks to save if there are changes.
column8: The question "Save changes?" with Cancel | Discard | Save, as in GNOME

column4: Reading and writing the original format is a requirement, but the guide does not describe it. The specification comes from outside sources and tests on the VM, as for .pages and .numbers.

Return in the navigator, the New (+) button, Slide > New Slide, Option-dragging a thumbnail (copies the slide) or Cmd-D. The new slide goes after the selected one, with the same theme and master. In a new document, the first slide uses Title & Subtitle and the second uses the second master of the theme.
column8: M+: the + button in the sidebar header and Ctrl+M (Ctrl+Shift+N is already New window in Desk)

column4: Dragging one or several images from the Finder or the Media Browser onto the navigator or the Light Table creates a slide per image.

An object pasted on another slide stays in the same position as the original. Whole slides are pasted after the selected slide. Paste keeps the text formatting, and Paste and Match Style takes that of the destination. Deleting with Delete does not put the object on the clipboard.

In the Navigator, Tab or dragging right indents the slide, to as many levels as wanted, but only one level beyond the slide above. Shift-Tab undoes it. The triangle collapses the group. Deleting the first slide of a collapsed group deletes the whole group, and in an open group the children move up a level. Indenting does not change playback.
Delete in the navigator, with Shift for several. Edit > Undo brings deleted slides back.
Slide > Skip Slide or the context menu, in any view, and an optional toolbar button. The slide stays in the document but does not appear in the presentation.
column8: Ctrl+Shift+H, as in today's Keynote, and Skip this slide in the Format pane with nothing selected

column4: Drag one or several slides in the Navigator, the Outline or the Light Table. Dragging the first slide of a group takes the group with it.

Per slide, in Slide Inspector > Appearance, or on the master, to number every new slide based on it. Slide > Show or Hide Slide Numbers on All Slides. The number can be moved and formatted, and skipped slides are not numbered.
column7: Partial: skipped slides left out of the count

column4: The Themes button opens the chooser with "Apply theme to" All Slides or Selected Slides and the option "Retain changes to theme defaults". Different themes can separate chapters of the same presentation. Format > Reapply Master to Slide goes back to the theme default.
column7: Partial: the theme as a set

column4: The Masters button or a thumbnail in Slide Inspector > Appearance. Style changes made on the slide stay, and Reapply Master to Slide removes them.
Checkboxes in Slide Inspector > Appearance turn the title, body, object placeholder and slide number on or off without changing the master.
Solid color, gradient, image or tinted image, with the scale options of the image fill.

column3: Change several slides through the master
column4: View > Show Masters and editing the master marked with the tick changes all the slides that use it.

Insert > Comment. They are always above the objects and can be moved, resized, hidden and deleted with the X. They appear on the presenter display but not to the audience, and there they cannot be moved or hidden. They print when they are visible.
A field below the slide canvas, shown or hidden from the View menu. Notes appear only on the presenter display and in rehearsal, and print with Slides with Notes. They are different from comments.

There are no paragraph, character or list styles, nor a Styles Drawer. The appearance comes from the master placeholder and direct formatting. Pasted text keeps its source formatting, and Paste and Match Style takes that of the destination.
Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough with its own color, shadow, outline (Format > Font > Outline), size in 1 pt steps, baseline, capitals, advanced typography and ligatures, as in Pages.
column7: Partial: shadow, font features and spacing, as in Pages

column4: Applies to title and body placeholders. When the text does not fit, the overflow indicator (+) appears below the box. A double click on the indicator, the checkbox in the format bar, the context menu or the Text Inspector turn it on. Font and line spacing shrink by 40% at most, and the Inspector shows how much they were reduced. The Fonts window, the Inspector and the rulers keep showing the original values, and text pasted into a box without the feature goes back to its original size. Can be turned on in the master.
column7: Partial: style:shrink-to-fit exists, the 40% limit does not

column4: Text Inspector > Bullets: none, a character with color, an app image, a custom image, numbering and tiered numbering, with Continue from Previous or Start At. Size as a percentage or "Scale with text", bullet indent, text indent and vertical alignment. "Number indent" creates the next level with another style. Free text boxes start without bullets, and the body of placeholders already has those of the theme.

The Text Box button and type. The box grows to the edge of the slide and then wraps the line. Only the width can be adjusted, and the height follows the text. On a master, the box appears on all slides based on it, like a copyright notice. Can be locked.

Every shape takes text, except lines, with an indicator when the text runs past the edge. Format > Shape > Reset Text and Object Handles makes the text horizontal after rotating the shape. Resizing a group does not change the text size.

Horizontal (Auto-align only in cells) and vertical alignment, line spacing from the format bar, space before and after the paragraph, character spacing, tabs and indents from the ruler, and inset in the Text Inspector.
column7: Partial: character spacing and the largest-space rule, as in Pages

column4: In text boxes and rectangular shapes. The format bar creates up to four equal columns, and the Text Inspector allows more columns, different widths and a gutter.
Checking while typing, from the cursor to the end of the presentation or only in the selection, Cmd-; and the Spelling window with a language per passage. There is no grammar checker.
Preferences > Auto-Correction: smart quotes, capitals, ordinal suffixes, email and URL links, list detection, automatic spelling correction, and a table of symbols and text.
Simple and Advanced, Replace All, Replace, Replace & Find, Next and Previous, Use Selection for Find and Jump to Selection.
As in Pages: double and triple click, Shift and Cmd for noncontiguous selections, Keyboard Viewer, Characters, accents and a nonbreaking space with Option-Space.
The guide does not mention hyphenation, unlike Pages. To be checked on the VM whether Keynote text never hyphenates.

Images in the QuickTime formats (TIFF, GIF, JPEG, PDF, PSD, EPS, PICT), mask, Instant Alpha, Adjust Image, predefined and free shapes with point editing, group, lock, connection lines, resize, flip and rotate, border, frame, shadow, reflection, opacity, fills and MathType 6 equations, as in Pages. There are no inline objects and no text wrap.
column7: Partial: as in Pages (frame and reflection are extensions)

column3: Scale down large images on import
column4: An image larger than the slide is scaled down to fit. JPEG stays JPEG, and the other formats become TIFF. After that, Original Size in the Metrics Inspector does not bring the resolution back. The General preference "Scale placed images to fit on slide" turns it off, and the guide suggests PDF for images whose size will change a lot.
Preferences > Rulers: horizontal and vertical lines, spacing as a percentage and their own color. They also appear on masters and do not print. Cmd while dragging hides guides and the grid.

Guides at the center and edges, for equal spacing between three or more objects and for equal size, with configurable colors. Fixed guides dragged from the rulers stay on the slide where they were made and do not appear in the presentation or in print. x and y position in the Metrics Inspector and a preference to show size and position when moving.
Format > Copy Style and Paste Style, from text to text and from object to object, tables and cells included.

An audio file or iTunes playlist dragged onto the slide or a media placeholder becomes a speaker icon, which disappears in the presentation. The sound plays only on that slide and stops on advance. The Start Audio and Stop Audio builds control when it starts and ends.

Document Inspector > Audio: a file or iTunes playlist dragged onto the Soundtrack well, played once or looped, with volume and a preview button. Starts with the presentation and plays to the end of the file or of the presentation. Changes to the iTunes playlist only count when it is dragged again.

Document Inspector > Audio > Record or File > Record Slideshow. The presentation runs from the chosen slide, with a blinking red icon, and records the voice and the moment of each advance. W (white screen), F (stop) and B (black screen) pause, any key resumes and Esc ends and saves. The presentation type becomes Recorded, and playback starts on the first recorded slide. Recording again offers Record and Replace, Record and Append and Record from Start, and Clear Recording sets the type back to Normal.
Drag from the Finder or the Media Browser onto the slide or a media placeholder, or Insert > Choose. Builds move the movie and start or stop it on a click.
Graphic Inspector > Stroke > Picture Frame, with style and width scale.

Start and end, poster frame, "Start movie on click" instead of when the slide opens, repeat (none, loop or back and forth) and volume, with controls for the preview. In the presentation, the controls appear when the pointer moves over the movie.

Format > Image > Reduce Media File Size trims the movie or sound to the part used and the image to its visible part. File > Reduce File Size does the same for the whole document. It cannot be undone, and not every movie takes it.

Slide Inspector > Transition: effect, duration, direction (when the effect has one) and options of some effects, such as Mosaic, Swap (Vertauschen) and Fade Through Color. Clicking the thumbnail shows the preview in the Inspector. The guide does not list the effects, and the full catalogue, with the options of each, comes from the menu on the VM.
Start transition On Click or Automatically, with the Delay that the slide stays on screen before the transition.

The same objects on successive slides move and resize to the position and size they have on the next slide. Applies to images, shapes and text boxes, and not to tables, charts and movies. The recommended technique is to duplicate the slide (Cmd-D), change the copy and apply the effect to the first slide of the pair. In the file, each pair of objects needs an identifier shared by the two slides, because xml:id is unique in the document.

Anagram (Anagramm), Shimmer (Schimmern), Sparkle (Funken) and Swing (Schwingen) take the letters of the text of one slide to the text of the next. They work best with short text, the same font and size, and letters in common, and for Anagram and Swing with the text in the same position.

Object Push (Objekt verschieben), Object Zoom, Perspective and Revolve (Rotieren) move all graphic elements together, as if they entered and left the slide. They work best with slides that have several large images.

Take the slide off the screen in three dimensions while the next comes in, regardless of the content. They may need a strong graphics card, and the menu sets apart the "Effects that can't play on this computer". Cube and Reflection may come out cropped with "Scale slides up to fit display", and two preferences reduce these effects to avoid cropping.
column7: Partial: effects without a name in SMIL

column4: Take one slide off and bring the next in the plane of the screen.
The menu keeps the last five effects used.

Build Inspector > Build In (Aufbau) and Build Out (Abbau): effect, direction (when the effect has one), delivery and duration, with a preview in the thumbnail. Applies to one or several objects, and an object can have several builds. Grouping or ungrouping objects removes their builds. The catalogue of effects comes from the menu on the VM.

Build Inspector > Action > Move. A red line joins the object to a transparent copy that marks the destination, off the slide too. The path can be straight or curved, with nodes and handles (Option-click adds a node), and "Add path" creates a new stretch, which is a separate build. The red diamond shows the paths again, and with Option they stay visible. Has acceleration. Applies to image, shape, text box, chart, movie, media and table.

Final opacity, rotation clockwise or counterclockwise by an angle (360° is one turn, and multiples give several) and scale up to 200%, each with acceleration and duration. Resizing or rotating the transparent copy of a Move combines these changes with the movement.

Insert > Smart Build > effect creates a blue box with a purple diamond, onto which photos are dragged from the Media Browser or the Finder. The editor changes the order, removes images, makes the size equal or keeps the relative size and adjusts the scale of the two modes of some effects. The box sets the largest size. Duration, the first and last image of the cycle, orientation and the time of each image are in the Inspector, and builds of other objects can come between the images.

The Build Order drawer (More Options) lists all the builds of the slide, and dragging changes the order. The Order menu of the Inspector does the same for the selected object. Clicking an item previews only that item.
Each build starts On Click (the default), Automatically After the previous one or item n, or Automatically With item n, which must be just above in the list. The delay goes up to 60 seconds.

All at Once, By Bullet, By Bullet Group (the bullet with its children), By Highlighted Bullet (only the last one stays highlighted) and By Paragraph, for text without bullets. Some effects animate by word or by letter. "Build from" and "Build to" choose a range of items.
All at Once, By Row, By Column, By Cell, By Row Content, Column Content or Cell Content (the empty table appears first), Bottom Up and Bottom Up by Content. All parts use the same effect.

All at Once, Background First (axes and then all the data), By Series, By Set, By Element in Series and By Element in Set. The legend has its own build and order, unless it is grouped with the chart first.
Items of a text, a table and a chart can interleave in the order, such as the first bullet, the first wedge of a pie and the second bullet. Needs "Set timing and order of each build".
column7: Partial: parts of tables and charts

column3: Start and stop movies and audio
column4: Without a build, the movie starts when the slide appears. Start Movie (build in) and Stop Movie (build out), and Start Audio and Stop Audio, control the moment, on a click or in sequence.
Format > Copy Animation and Paste Animation, only between compatible object types (Typewriter is for text only). Delete from the drawer with Delete or by choosing None as the effect.

Hyperlink Inspector > "Enable as a hyperlink" on text, an image or a shape. The object gets a curved blue arrow, visible only while editing, and the text is underlined in the presentation too. Themes come with ready-made forward and back arrows.

The Webpage destination with a URL, opened in the default browser of the computer running the presentation. Typed addresses become links by the preference of the computer, not of the document. "Display" changes the link text.
The Email Message destination with recipient and subject, opened in the default email program. "Display" is disabled when the link is an object.

The Slide destination: next, previous, first, last, last viewed or a slide number. To be checked on the VM whether a link to a number follows the slide when the order changes. In ODP, the link points to the name of the slide.
The Exit Slideshow destination, for a button or text that stops the show.
The Keynote File destination, chosen in a dialog. The other presentation plays from its first slide.

Document Inspector > Presentation > Links Only. Slides change only through hyperlinks, and the pointer appears on slides that have hyperlinks. The preference "Show pointer when using the mouse" makes it appear always, and the password to exit keeps the audience from leaving.
Text links start underlined, which the preference "Underline text hyperlinks when created" turns off. The U button of the format bar or the Fonts window removes or adds the underline.

The 11 types of Pages and Numbers. The data are in the Data Editor, a table that does not appear on the slide, with Add Row and Add Column, labels that can be dragged to reorder, pasting from Excel or AppleWorks, and Swap Rows and Columns. The chart starts with sample data and the appearance of the theme, and Option-clicking Charts lets the user draw it at the size wanted.

A chart copied from Numbers keeps its link to the tables of the source document. Refresh rereads the data, and the Numbers document must be saved before copying and after each edit. Unlink turns the chart into a plain chart, edited in the Data Editor, and the Source link opens the Numbers document.
Title, legend, text, size and rotation (2D only), axes, colors and textures, value labels, error bars, trendlines, pie, bar, line, area, scatter, mixed, 2-axis and 3D scene, as in Pages.
column7: Partial: as in Pages (label every N, distance of pie labels, beveled edges)

column4: The Table button or Insert > Table creates a 3 × 3 table with the theme style, with or without headers depending on the theme. Option-clicking Table draws the table, and the number of rows and columns follows the size. Rows, columns, headers and footers are in the format bar.

column3: Paste a table from Pages or Numbers
column4: The pasted table becomes a Keynote table. Rows and columns hidden in Numbers and Numbers cell comments do not come.
Dragging selected cells out of the table creates a new table with them. Option-dragging copies cells to another table, and dragging within the table swaps the values.
Up to five header rows, five header columns and five footer rows. New rows at the end go above the footer, and at the start, below the header.
As in Pages: Tab, arrows, Cmd-Return, "Return key moves to next cell" in the Table Inspector, autofill and Clear All.
Alternating row colors, row and column size, merge and split, borders, cell background with color, gradient, image or tinted image, and Copy and Paste Style.
column6: TAB-04, TAB-13, TAB-14, TAB-22 to TAB-25

column4: Ascending or descending by the chosen column.

Rules with a fixed value or a cell reference, text color and style and fill, and the highest rule wins for each attribute. Copy and paste takes the rules to cells of another table, and Select All finds the cells with the same rules.
Automatic, Number, Currency, Percentage, Date and Time, Duration, Fraction, Numeral System, Scientific, Text and custom ones, without the Numbers cell controls.
column7: Partial: bases, duration and flexible space

column4: The iWork formulas and functions, described in the formulas guide and not in the user guide. References stay in the same table, and headers make formulas readable.
Document Inspector > Presentation: Normal (advances on a click or a key, the default), Links Only (KLNK-07), Recorded (KOBJ-08) and Self-Playing.

Runs by itself like a movie, without interaction, for kiosks. Automatic transitions and builds play as usual, and those that would wait for a click start after the Transitions and Builds delays of the Document Inspector, which apply to all. Esc still ends it, unless there is a password to exit. Does not use the presenter display.
Automatically play upon open, Loop slideshow, Restart show if idle for n minutes and Require password to exit show (KDOC-15).
column7: Partial: play upon open and restart if idle

column3: Slide size and fit to the screen
column4: Document Inspector > Slide Size, with 800 × 600 and 1024 × 768 for projectors and 1920 × 1080 in HD themes. A slide smaller than the screen plays centered with a black border, and a larger one is scaled down. The preference "Scale slides up to fit display" scales the presentation without changing the document, with some loss of quality.
The Play button, from the selected slide. A click, the right arrow or space advance, and Esc or Q end. In a recorded presentation, H pauses everything, sound included.
column8: F5 plays, as does the Play button of the header bar; Ctrl+Alt+P is already Insert, Choose

column4: Play > Rehearse Slideshow shows the presenter display on a single monitor, with the current slide, the next one, the notes (U and D scroll) and whatever is turned on in Preferences. Esc leaves.

With mirroring, the same on both screens. Without it, the presentation goes to the primary or the secondary monitor (Preferences > Slideshow), and the other shows the presenter display. X swaps the screens during the presentation.

Preferences > Presenter Display and Play > Customize Presenter Display: current slide, build markers (blue dots), next slide, ready to advance indicator (red or green bar), notes, clock and a timer of time remaining (with a maximum duration) or elapsed. The items are dragged and resized. During the presentation, the top of the display has Slides (thumbnails and Go To), Black, Options (swap displays, fit to screen, customize) and Help.

F freezes, B shows a black screen, W a white screen and H hides the presentation and shows the last program (on Lion in full screen, ends it). N, space, Return, the right or down arrow and Page Down advance one build, and Shift-down arrow or Shift-Page Down go to the next slide. The left or up arrow, P, Delete and Page Up go back to the start of the slide's builds or to the previous slide, and Shift-left arrow goes back one build. A number and Return go straight to the slide, and =, + or - open the slide switcher, which does not reach skipped slides. ? or / show the keys, and Esc, Cmd-period or period end.
With the preference for controls on pointer hover, the movie shows controls, except when it is small. K pauses and resumes, J goes back, L goes forward, I goes to the start and O to the end.
A preference shows the pointer only on slides with hyperlinks or movies, or whenever the mouse moves. C hides the pointer.

Apple Remote (play, pause, forward, back, first and last slide, slide switcher and volume) and the Keynote Remote app on iPhone or iPod touch, paired by code on the same Wi-Fi network. In Desk, the starting point is the keys of USB clickers (Page Up, Page Down, B), and the Keynote Remote protocol is left out.

A preference lets Exposé, Dashboard and other programs use the screen, with a possible loss of performance. Hyperlinks to the web, email or a file pause the presentation, which comes back from the Keynote icon in the Dock.

From and To range, and Keynote in the Copies & Pages menu: Individual Slides, Slides with Notes, Outline (titles and bullets only, without free text boxes) and Handouts (several slides per page, with Draft Quality). Options: only the selected slides, without backgrounds and fills (light text prints black), each stage of builds, skipped slides, borders, numbers, date, 3D charts at high resolution and margins. Comments print when they are visible.
Save As > "Save a copy as" iWork '08, with the option to copy audio and movies. New '09 transitions and effects may be lost.

Share > Export > QuickTime, with all transitions and builds. Manual Advance, Hyperlinks Only, Recorded Timing or Fixed Timing (duration per slide and per build stage, and repeat none, loop or back and forth). Full screen on open, formats (high quality, CD-ROM, web or custom), audio (soundtrack or narration) and transparency. With a soundtrack a second file with only the sound also comes out, and in a self-playing presentation the end of the soundtrack ends the movie. In Desk, the equivalent is a video with fixed or recorded timing, and the interactive movie depends on QuickTime.
Share > Export > PPT. Bulleted text may be lost, and a body hidden from the Slide Inspector leaves the outline. PowerPoint has no alpha channel, so frames may cover what is behind them.
Export > PDF, with the print options, for reading on screen and without margins. For printing, the guide recommends Print > Save as PDF. Hyperlinks stay active.
JPEG (with quality), PNG or TIFF, of all slides or a range, and optionally one image per build stage. The files come out numbered (name.001, name.002).
All slides or a selection, an optional image per build stage, links to the first, previous and next slide, and the format and quality of the images.
Share > Send via Email attaches a Keynote, PowerPoint or PDF version in Mail. Documents with a password go protected, and PDF and PowerPoint have no password.

column3: YouTube, iDVD, iPhoto, iWeb, iTunes, iPod and GarageBand
column4: Sending directly as a video or an album, with recorded or fixed timing and optional audio. The video itself is covered by KEXP-03.

column4: Showing the presentation in an iChat video chat.
Publishing for viewing in the browser, without recorded narration, self-playing and some effects.
column7: Out of scope: service shut down

column4: View > Show Masters opens the list of masters above the Navigator (KINT-07). With a master selected, the Slide Inspector becomes that of the master (Folienvorlage), with the Appearance pane (placeholders, background and layers) and the Transition pane.

The guide suggests a test slide with the master being edited, switching between the two to adjust tabs, line spacing and outline levels. Format > Reapply Master to Slide undoes what the slide changed, such as the background, and Reapply Master to Selection (Auswahl wieder an die Vorlage anpassen) does the same with whatever is selected.

With the master selected, the New button, Slide > New Master, Return or Edit > Duplicate create the copy, renamed with a double click on the name. The guide recommends duplicating before changing, to keep the original available.

With both presentations open, dragging a slide from one Navigator to the other brings the slide and its master, which goes at the end of the list. Dragging a master between the lists of masters brings only the master. In ODP, the internal name of the master is unique, so the imported one gets another style:name when the name already exists and keeps the visible name in style:display-name.

A new master starts from the theme's Blank, or from any master emptied with Select All and Delete. A new theme starts from a presentation with all masters deleted except Blank. The guide recommends defining text and background first, testing the layouts with long text, and duplicating the first master so that the others inherit text and background.

The Title and Body (Text) checkboxes of the Appearance pane turn on the two placeholders, with free size and position. Text Inspector > Bullets sets whether the body starts with bullets, numbering or plain text, and formatting the sample text sets the appearance of up to five outline levels.
column7: Native (presentation:class title and outline, with presentation styles per level)

column3: Text box or shape as a text placeholder
column4: A text box or shape on the master becomes a placeholder with Define as Text Placeholder, in the Appearance pane or in Format > Advanced. The guide does not say how it behaves on the slide, which is to be checked on the VM.
column7: Partial: link between the master placeholder and the box on the slide

column4: An image or shape on the master becomes a placeholder with Define as Media Placeholder, with an optional tag (Attribut) and its own size, mask and position. An image, sound or movie dragged onto it on the slide takes its position and size. In ODP, the media placeholder is native (presentation:class="graphic"), unlike ODT and ODS.
column7: Partial: mask by shape and frame, as in Pages

column4: The Object Placeholder (Objektplatzhalter) checkbox marks where tables, charts, web views and imported images go. Such an object added to a slide of the master takes the position and size of the placeholder. The guide mentions web views (Webdarstellungen) but does not describe them, and they are to be checked on the VM.

A logo, text, shape, image, sound, movie, table or chart put on the master appears on every slide that uses it, and Arrange > Lock keeps it from being moved by accident. Groups of masters with different backgrounds can mark parts of the presentation, and images with an alpha channel let the background show under the objects of the slide.
The Background controls of the Appearance pane give a color, gradient, image or tinted image, as on the slide (KSLD-12).

column3: Layers between the slide and the master
column4: The option of the Appearance pane that lets slide objects interact with the layers of the master (Objekte auf der Folie interagieren mit den Ebenen der Vorlage) interleaves the objects of the two in the layer order. Without it, the master always stays behind. The exact effect of Bring to Front and Send to Back is to be checked on the VM.
Guides dragged from the rulers on the master, horizontal from the top ruler and vertical from the left, appear on every slide based on it. The grid of Preferences also appears on masters (KOBJ-03).

On a test slide, format a text box or shape and use Format > Advanced > Define Text (or Shape) for the current master or for all masters. The defaults of a master apply on its slides, and those of all apply in the whole document.
Shadow, reflection, opacity and border color that every imported image gets, defined the same way, per master or for all.

The number of rows and columns, line styles and colors, text styles and shadow of the table that the Table button creates, per master or for all. Each attribute applies to a whole area (header row, header column, inner borders and outer borders), as in Pages.
Style, size and position of each chart type, defined one type at a time, per master or for all.

The Transition pane of the master has effect, direction, duration, start (on click or automatic) and delay, like that of the slide, and the slides based on it make this transition. The page style of the master takes the same attributes in ODF, but the standard does not say that slides inherit them, so each slide writes its own transition.

Builds created on the master, such as bullets that come in one by one, apply on every slide based on it. ODF takes animations on the master, but they only reach the objects of the master itself, and not the body of each slide.

All the masters, with placeholders, backgrounds, guides, transitions and builds, and the defaults of text, shape, image, table and chart. File > Save Theme (KDOC-10) can copy audio and movies inside, which makes the file larger. The theme goes in the user's Themes folder, the Chooser lists only what is there, and a theme saved elsewhere opens from the Finder. In Desk Slides, the folder is in the user's data directory (XDG), as in Desk Writer.
column7: Partial: defaults per object type and per master

column4: File > Choose Theme with the original theme and slide size, "Retain changes to theme defaults" unchecked and applied to all slides or only the selected ones (KSLD-09).

The window works on the minimum screen of 1280 × 720 and adapts to smaller windows, such as half a screen: the sidebar and then the Inspector become overlay panes, and the object buttons of the header bar go into the Insert menu, as in Desk Writer. Phones and screens smaller than the minimum are not supported.
column8: M+: as in Desk Writer (GNM-01)

column4: Notices that need no answer appear in a toast, with Undo when the action can be undone.

column3: Unsaved documents at the end of the session
column4: With a changed and unsaved document, the app holds back the end of the session and shutdown until the person decides.
Slides, objects, presenter notes and the running presentation appear in the accessibility tree, with role, name, description and alternative text.
A thumbnailer shows the first screen of .key and ODP documents in Files, without needing LibreOffice.
A LocalSearch extractor indexes the text and the information (author, title, keywords) of .key and ODP documents.
The GNOME Shell search lists the recent documents of the app and opens the chosen one in it.
Text in Hebrew, Persian and Arabic runs from right to left in boxes and bullets, and the interface mirrors in these languages.
The interface is translated into the languages of po/LANGUAGES.md.

View is the menu of the Sidebar button and Insert sits beside it in the header bar, Format and Arrange are in the Format pane and the context menu, and the main menu holds only the file and the application, as in Desk Writer. A command search finds any item by name.
column8: M+: as in Desk Writer (GNM-10); Slide becomes the context menu of the navigator, and Play, the menu of the Play button

column4: The shortcuts dialog is that of Libadwaita, and the iWork shortcuts that clash with those of GNOME are changed, as in Desk Writer (STY-04, OBJ-22).
During the presentation, the app prevents the screensaver and suspend (gtk_application_inhibit) and puts the presenter display on the other monitor through GNOME.

A pane the height of the window, on the left. The content switcher chooses between Navigator, Outline, Masters, Comments and Search results, and the + button creates a slide from a master. F9 shows and hides it, as in Desk Writer.
There is no bottom bar: a zoom control sits over a corner of the slide, and the presenter notes open under the slide from the View menu, as in Desk Writer (GNM-13).

column3: Notice of a screen smaller than the minimum
column4: When a window opens on a monitor with fewer than 1280 × 720 logical pixels (after the display scale), a bar under the top bars says that the screen is below the Desk minimum resolution and that parts of the window may not fit. The application keeps working, and the Close button hides the bar until the next launch. As in Desk Writer.
column8: M+: as in Desk Writer (GNM-14)

column4: Edit > Deselect All (Shift-Cmd-A) clears the selection of objects and slides.
column8: Ctrl+Shift+A, as in Desk Writer

column4: Preferences > General > Animations: "Include obsolete animations in choices" adds the old effects to the menus (44 transitions, 33 build ins and 32 build outs in place of 27, 28 and 27). When it is off, they leave the menus and keep playing in presentations that already use them.

column3: Chart and legend geometry on masters
column4: Format > Advanced > Define Chart and Legend Geometry for All Masters takes the size and position of the selected chart and legend to all masters (KMES-17).
View > Zoom > Fit in Window shows the whole slide in the space available and follows the size of the window.
Insert > Column Break continues the text in the next column of a text box or shape with columns (KTXT-08).
